title: Plans for a tour and clearing up the 1959 band lineup
summary: He expects a tour with Barry Martin's band, asks after Sammy Rimington, and confirms six men went to Europe in 1959.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Do you have any plans for, do you foresee that you will be going on any more tours?

Well, I'm expecting a tour next year. That's why I say I want to take my time and build myself up strong like I want to be. Cause Barry Martin is working up a deal for me to make a tour with his band. Cause a lot of my friends over there in England and in Italy and Brussels, people I've never seen. But they've all heard of me and they've heard my records, heard the records of me. They all would like for him to make some kind of arrangement. That he could bring me over there. And that's what he's been writing to me about where he'll be down here in June.
Yeah, he's supposed to be on that jazz fest. Oh.

And if I can make it, I'll try to be on it. Is Simon Richardson coming here? I don't know. Because I haven't received one letter from Sammy Remington. Since he went back to England, but I heard he moved to Denmark. Yeah.
I think that was the last letter I got from him. Or somebody wrote and told me that they saw him in Denmark.
When you were on this tour in Europe in 59, didn't Sammy go with you and play you for a bit on that?
I thought you said, no, maybe you... No, not with the George Lewis group. I'm thinking of a different time, I think. I think there was a time...
Because we didn't even have a banjo player. Oh. No. Only six of us went over at first time in 59. Right.
